title: Stream a cited Chat response
description: Use the modern Platform Chat API to send a permission-aware question, continue the conversation, and read server-sent events with the official TypeScript API client's createStream EventStream.

codeWalkthrough.intro: The runnable scaffold uses glean.chat.createStream, the published Glean auth package, and the official API client. Every turn iterates a typed EventStream.

examples.title: Configure the Platform API client
examples.description: Resolve the backend from work email or an explicit server URL, then construct Glean with a refreshable OAuth token provider or GLEAN_API_TOKEN, plus includeExperimental.

examples.title: Iterate createStream events
examples.description: Call glean.chat.createStream and for-await the typed EventStream. Write RESPONSE_OUTPUT_TEXT_DELTA.data.delta and keep RESPONSE_COMPLETED.data.response for citations.

examples.title: Continue a conversation and render citations
examples.description: Store the first turn, pass its conversation_id to a follow-up, and render citation sources and snippets from the completed response.

prerequisites: A Glean instance with content indexed
Your work email, or the complete Glean backend HTTPS origin
A tenant that permits this public OAuth client and chat scope through DCR; an administrator-provisioned OAuth client or user-scoped CHAT token is the fallback

demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Returns a non-empty permission-aware streamed response with a conversation_id and at least one citation source when the user's indexed content contains a relevant policy.

codeAssets.description: TypeScript CLI using the modern Platform Chat API, OAuth, citations, and createStream EventStream iteration

steps.title: Scaffold the project
steps.description: Copies the runnable TypeScript Chat CLI and fixture tests into a new directory. OAuth login and secure token storage come from the pinned @gleanwork/auth package.

steps.title: Run the fixture tests
steps.description: Runs Vitest with MSW-backed fixtures, without credentials or live network access, covering typed createStream events, conversation_id propagation, and citations.

steps.title: Sign in with OAuth
steps.description: Discovers your Glean backend from work email and completes Authorization Code with PKCE for Chat and offline_access. Use --server-url for an explicit backend, GLEAN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID for an administrator-provisioned public client, or GLEAN_API_TOKEN as a user-scoped fallback.

steps.title: Stream one Chat turn
steps.description: Sends a question through createStream, then prints delta text, conversation_id, and grounded citation data against your own instance.

steps.title: Stream a follow-up
steps.description: Starts a stored conversation, iterates createStream events, and sends a follow-up using the returned conversation_id.

questions.prompt: What is your work email address?
What question do you want to ask about content in your Glean instance?
What follow-up question should use the same conversation?

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the verified Streaming Chat with citations quickstart. Ask for the user's work email and a question about content in their Glean instance. Run the fixture tests, sign in with @gleanwork/auth through DCR OAuth using the chat scope, then stream one Platform Chat turn. Use @gleanwork/api-client 0.20.2 with includeExperimental enabled. Call glean.chat.createStream() for every turn and for-await RESPONSE_OUTPUT_TEXT_DELTA and RESPONSE_COMPLETED events. Do not call create(), do not set stream on create(), do not use CreateAcceptEnum or Accept-header workarounds, and do not parse SSE by hand. Pass conversation_id from the stored first turn to the follow-up. Do not use legacy glean.client.chat, hand-roll Glean request construction, or expose credentials.
llmContext: Use Platform Chat API at /api/chat through @gleanwork/api-client 0.20.2. Every turn calls glean.chat.createStream(), which returns a typed EventStream. Do not call create() and do not set stream on create(). HTTP clients still send stream:true in the JSON body; SDK users call createStream() instead. Streaming events use event names RESPONSE_OUTPUT_TEXT_DELTA (data.delta) and RESPONSE_COMPLETED (data.response). Citations are content annotations with sources and optional snippets. OAuth or user-scoped CHAT token remains the permission boundary. Enable experimental features through includeExperimental; do not claim the API is stable.

content.problem: A first Chat integration needs more than a request and a string: it must preserve the user's permissions, continue a conversation, and consume streamed events correctly. This quickstart shows the modern Platform Chat API with the official TypeScript client's createStream EventStream.
takeItFurther: Render citation spans as links in a web interface using annotation start_index and end_index.
Persist conversation_id in an application session and resume it on the next request.
Add cancellation with AbortController when the Chat interaction moves into a UI.

limitations.title: Experimental API
limitations.description: Platform Chat is experimental and may change. The scaffold opts in explicitly through the SDK constructor.

limitations.title: createStream is SDK-only
limitations.description: HTTP clients request SSE by setting stream to true in the JSON body. SDK callers use createStream() instead of setting stream on create().

limitations.title: OAuth policy varies by tenant
limitations.description: DCR may be disabled or restricted, or may not grant Chat. Use an administrator-provisioned public client when available; a user-scoped CHAT token is the tutorial fallback.
